preamble: Depalatalization of the palatalized lateral [lʲ] to a plain lateral [l]. In West Slavic it came with the loss of the old hard/soft lateral contrast. In Czech the hard and soft l merged into a single 'middle' l around the turn of the 14th and 15th centuries. In Polish the soft lʲ became plain [l] while the hard ł became [w], so Old Polish las /lʲas/ is now /las/. Ukrainian depalatalized consonants before /e/, so the Proto-Slavic *l in *ležati 'to lie' is plain in лежати.

examples.note: The soft lateral lost its palatalization; the old hard ł became [w], leaving l as the only lateral.
